title: Five smooth stones (1 Samuel 17)
hookLine: a shepherd boy with a sling and no armor faces a giant

lines: CHOOSE A MAN, AND LET HIM COME.
cards: Two armies on two mountains, a valley between them.

Morning and evening, a Philistine champion named Goliath walks out into that valley in a bronze helmet and a coat of mail, with a spear like a weaver's beam, and shouts: choose a man, and let him come down to me.
Saul and all Israel are dismayed and greatly afraid. Into this walks the youngest son of Jesse, sent by his father to bring bread to his older brothers at the front.
He hears the challenge, and asks: who is this, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

teach.h: THE LION, THE BEAR, THE LAMB.
teach.b: His oldest brother, Eliab, is furious: why did you come down here? I know your pride. But word reaches Saul, and David says: your servant will go and fight him.
You're a boy, says Saul, and he's been a man of war since his youth. David answers from experience. When a lion or a bear took a lamb from the flock, I went after it and took the lamb from its mouth.
The LORD who saved me from the lion and the bear will save me from this Philistine.
So Saul dresses David in his own armor: a bronze helmet, a coat of mail, a sword. David tries to walk, and can't. I haven't tried these, he says, and takes them off.
This is the heart of the story. He doesn't go out in the king's equipment, pretending to be a soldier. He goes out as what he is.
He takes his staff, and "chose him five smooth stones out of the brook," puts them in his shepherd's bag, sling in hand. Goliath mocks him.

teach.h: IN THE NAME OF THE LORD OF HOSTS.
teach.b: David answers: you come to me with a sword and a spear, "but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts," for the battle is the LORD's.

teach.h: HE PICKED FIVE, AND NEEDED ONE.
teach.b: He runs toward the Philistine, takes one stone, slings it, and it sinks into Goliath's forehead, and he falls on his face. The text even notes there was no sword in David's hand.

teach.h: FIVE SMOOTH STONES OUT OF THE BROOK.
teach.b: He picked five, and needed one.

how: Jews read David and Goliath as part of the Former Prophets, and many readers take it as a story of courage and of trust in God.

games.q: you're David. the king has just dressed you in his own helmet, coat of mail and sword, and you can barely walk. what do you do?
o: wear it anyway; it's the king's armor.
take it off, and go with your staff, your sling and stones from the brook.
ask for a smaller set of armor.
games.why: he says he hasn't tried them, takes them off, and chooses five smooth stones out of the brook. he faces the giant as a shepherd, not a soldier.

practice: Name one giant in your valley right now, a debt, a hard conversation, a project you can't start, and notice whether you've been fighting it in someone else's armor.
Then ask what your smooth stones are, the small things you already know how to do, and choose one. If you pray, bring the giant to God as David did.
